policy: Discovery only. Entries are not ground truth and are not part of the frozen holdout until independently verified, pinned, mapped, hashed, and curated.

candidates.data_kind: source-level MCP servers with benign and malicious directories
candidates.notes: Peer-reviewed-paper companion. Likely the strongest new static-source candidate; must inspect overlap, language mix, exact benign count, and per-PoC mappings before admission.
Strong explicit labels but not static source artifacts. Keep outside source precision until a trace analyzer exists.
Includes confused deputy, audit tampering, SSRF, tool poisoning, and squatting.
Newly published dataset; schema, provenance, generation method, and overlap remain to be checked.
Potential MCP06 hard cases; determine whether records contain source, metadata, or runtime-only prompts.
Potential MCP02/MCP11/MCP16 coverage; requires exact taxonomy mapping.

candidates.data_kind: curated incident records with primary references
candidates.notes: Useful for finding original artifacts such as malicious npm MCP packages, but incident rows are not source labels themselves.
Do not count until the authors publish the promised underlying records.
Never use as SOT without independent manual validation.

candidates.data_kind: Python MCP source fixtures with explicit vulnerable and benign-control directories
candidates.notes: Strong MCP03 positives and hard negatives. Labels were authored for Agentinel, so reserve for external evaluation only after file-level mapping and overlap review. Do not treat the 35-server risk catalog as vulnerability ground truth.

candidates.data_kind: JavaScript MCP source/manifest fixtures with expected rule and clean-control assertions
candidates.notes: Useful after TypeScript/JavaScript support: overlaps MCP01, MCP03, MCP04, MCP05, and MCP13. Borderline project is particularly valuable for precision, but must remain untouched until holdout admission.

candidates.data_kind: Python and JavaScript intentionally vulnerable MCP servers with per-server vulnerability documentation
candidates.notes: Direct mappings include MCP01, MCP03, MCP04, MCP05, MCP06, and MCP09. No explicit clean corpus, so this contributes recall labels but not precision negatives.

candidates.data_kind: Python MCP challenge source with one documented vulnerability class per challenge plus a multi-vector case
candidates.notes: Public challenge documentation explicitly maps prompt injection, tool poisoning, scope, rug pull, shadowing, indirect injection, token theft, code execution, remote command injection, and a multi-vector chain. Pin revision and map only scanner-supported static labels before admission.

candidates.data_kind: Python/JavaScript source fixtures paired with expected.json results
candidates.notes: Includes true and negative command-execution lookalikes, including regex.exec and Python method-exec controls. Map expected rule IDs rather than directory names.

candidates.data_kind: MCP server source with expected JSON regression labels and behavior-mismatch controls
candidates.notes: Potentially valuable for MCP03 description-versus-implementation and multi-file parsing. Requires exact expected-label mapping and duplicate check against already acquired MCPTox/MSB material.

candidates.data_kind: Python/JavaScript/config MCP fixtures with vulnerable and clean directory labels
candidates.notes: Overlaps command injection, tool metadata injection, secrets, mutable dependencies, and configuration risks. File-level labels must be reconstructed from tests before admission.

candidates.data_kind: Explicitly labeled prompt-injection conversations including MCP tool responses
candidates.notes: Useful for MCP06 runtime/output analysis, but not static MCP source precision. Keep separate until the analyzer accepts transcript/tool-result artifacts.

candidates.data_kind: Registry tool metadata with risk-category classifier outputs
candidates.notes: Large metadata index with source repository links, but its classifications are automated and are not vulnerability SOT. Use only to locate artifacts for independent labeling.
